hunks.baseline: “Report. From your own mouth.”
hunks.sol: “Report it. Tell me yourself.”

hunks.baseline: The cold voice froze everyone inside the tent. Every last one of them was a senior of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, a master who had spent long years roaming the martial world.
hunks.sol: The cold voice froze everyone inside the tent. Every last one of them was a senior figure in the Mount Heng Sword Sect, a master who had spent long years roaming the martial world.

hunks.baseline: “The only survivors are twenty-three of us, including me. We have no idea whether the rest are alive or dead.”
hunks.sol: “There are only twenty-three survivors, including me. We don’t know whether the rest are alive or dead.”

hunks.baseline: A heavy silence settled over those present.
hunks.sol: A heavy silence settled over the gathering.

hunks.baseline: Some two hundred troops had been killed or captured, and they had lost three Peak masters. That alone would have made it hard to avoid punishment, but there was a bigger problem still.
hunks.sol: Some two hundred troops had been killed or captured, and they had lost three Peak masters. That alone would have made punishment unavoidable, but there was an even bigger problem.

hunks.baseline: “…To wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s branches and advance as far as Jeongyang.”
hunks.sol: “…To wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s branch and advance as far as Jeongyang.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. They said Jopil, One Question, One Kill, had chased Jin Taekyung all the way to Honju and captured him. But…”
hunks.sol: “Yes. I was told that Jopil, One Question, One Kill, had chased Jin Taekyung all the way to Honju and captured him. But…”

hunks.baseline: “He must have said the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s pursuit party was on his heels and asked you to help him.”
hunks.sol: “He said the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s pursuit party was on his heels and asked you to help him.”

hunks.baseline: “Who delivered that information?”
hunks.sol: “Who gave you that information?”

hunks.baseline: “Do you still think that?”
hunks.sol: “Do you still believe it?”

hunks.baseline: Smack!
hunks.sol: *Smack!*

hunks.baseline: Lee Seogwang’s head snapped to the side. Lee Cheonbaek’s gaze poured down on him like fire.
hunks.sol: Lee Seogwang’s head snapped to the side. Lee Cheonbaek glared down at him, his gaze blazing.

hunks.baseline: In the end, Lee Seogwang was ordered back to the Mount Heng Sword Sect, and with his withdrawal, the matter was settled for now. It was time to look at reality with a cool head.
hunks.sol: In the end, Lee Seogwang was ordered to return to the Mount Heng Sword Sect. Once he withdrew, the matter was settled for the time being.
Now it was time to assess the situation with a cool head.

hunks.baseline: “What is the situation?”
hunks.sol: “What is our current position?”

hunks.baseline: “We lost two hundred men, but more than half of them were wandering martial artists we scraped together in a hurry. The damage isn’t as bad as it sounds. The problem is…”
hunks.sol: “We lost two hundred men, but more than half were wandering martial artists we scraped together in a hurry. The damage isn’t as severe as it sounds. The problem is…”

hunks.baseline: It left a bitter taste in Lee Cheonbaek’s mouth. The Mount Heng Twin Devils, who had stood with him for twenty years. And Jopil, whom he had paid a fortune to hire, was dead as well.
hunks.sol: The thought left a bitter taste in Lee Cheonbaek’s mouth. The Mount Heng Twin Devils had stood beside him for twenty years, and Jopil, whom he had paid a fortune to hire, was dead as well.

hunks.baseline: A Peak master was someone who could change the course of a battle. Somehow, they had to fill the void.
hunks.sol: A Peak master could change the course of a battle. Somehow, they had to fill the void.

hunks.baseline: “The expense is already too high. By now, word of what happened in Honju will have spread, so they’ll try to drive their prices up.”
hunks.sol: “The expense is already too high. By now, word of what happened in Honju will have spread, so they’ll try to drive up their prices.”

hunks.baseline: “They aren’t trustworthy men, either. Especially the mounted bandits. Aren’t they human butchers? If we hire people like that, our sect’s reputation will suffer afterward…”
hunks.sol: “They aren’t trustworthy, either. Especially the mounted bandits. Aren’t they human butchers? If we hire men like that, our sect’s reputation afterward…”

hunks.baseline: “There are no fewer than five hundred men gathered here. We have more than twice their numbers, and we aren’t behind in Peak masters either.”
hunks.sol: “There are no fewer than five hundred men gathered here. We outnumber them by more than two to one, and we aren’t behind in the number of Peak masters either.”

hunks.baseline: “My son thought the same thing. Then he got utterly wrecked in Honju.”
hunks.sol: “My son thought the same thing. Then he got utterly crushed in Honju.”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t worry about whether they’re human butchers or anything else. Throw everything we have into this. If we lose this war, it won’t be our reputation we lose—it’ll be our lives!”
hunks.sol: “Forget whether they’re human butchers or anything else. Throw everything we have into this. If we lose this war, it won’t be our reputation we lose—it’ll be our lives!”

hunks.baseline: At Lee Cheonbaek’s thunderous command, the seniors realized persuasion was pointless. That did not mean the discussion was over.
hunks.sol: At Lee Cheonbaek’s thunderous command, the seniors realized that trying to persuade him was pointless. But that did not mean the discussion was over.

hunks.baseline: “The defeat at Honju is one thing, but they’re shaken by the news that Jin Taekyung killed Jopil, One Question, One Kill.”
hunks.sol: “The defeat at Honju is one thing, but they’re also shaken by the news that Jin Taekyung killed Jopil, One Question, One Kill.”

hunks.baseline: *Are there really people stupid enough to believe a rumor that dumb?*
hunks.sol: *Are there really fools stupid enough to believe such an absurd rumor?*

hunks.baseline: As if it weren’t enough that that pathetic fool Jin Taekyung had poisoned his son, now he had supposedly killed a Peak master too. The scheme was obvious. Lee Cheonbaek’s teeth clenched at the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s despicable tactics.
hunks.sol: As if it weren’t enough that the pathetic fool Jin Taekyung had poisoned his son, now he had supposedly killed a Peak master too. The scheme was obvious. The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s despicable tactics made Lee Cheonbaek grind his teeth.

hunks.baseline: “Find everyone spreading that kind of nonsense. Don’t miss a single one!”
hunks.sol: “Find everyone spreading that nonsense. Don’t miss a single one!”

hunks.baseline: If he took a few heads as examples, morale might drop, but he could keep the army from collapsing. Now was the time to clamp down and push forward.
hunks.sol: Taking a few heads as examples might hurt morale further, but it would keep the army from collapsing. Now was the time to clamp down and push forward.

hunks.baseline: That was how the debts and grudges of Murim worked. The chain of debts and grudges would not break until one of the two sides fell.
hunks.sol: That was how the debts and grudges of Murim worked. Their chain would not break until one of the two sides fell.

hunks.baseline: The physician was astounded. It was my second day since I’d come to. Overnight, the scabs had fallen away, and pale new skin had grown in.
hunks.sol: The physician clicked his tongue in amazement. It was the second day since I’d regained consciousness, and overnight, the scabs had fallen away to reveal smooth new skin.

hunks.baseline: “In ten years as a physician, this is the first time I’ve seen anything like this.”
hunks.sol: “In ten years as a physician, I’ve never seen anything like this.”

hunks.baseline: Even to me, the speed of it was astonishing. The flesh melted by the heat of Flame Divine Palm, the fractured bones, the deep sword wounds—there was no trace of them left.
hunks.sol: Even to me, the speed of my recovery was astonishing. The flesh melted by the heat of Flame Divine Palm, the fractured bones, the deep sword wounds—there was no trace of them left.

hunks.baseline: There was only one method in the real world that produced a similar result.
hunks.sol: There was only one method in the real world that could produce similar results.

hunks.baseline: Healing magic used by the tiny handful of Hunters known as healers.
hunks.sol: Healing magic, used by the tiny handful of Hunters known as healers.

hunks.baseline: *Is complete healing too much to ask?*
hunks.sol: *Was a full recovery too much to hope for?*

hunks.baseline: I was a little disappointed, but it was just as well. If a single level-up had healed every wound on my body, it would have been hard to dodge suspicion.
hunks.sol: I was a little disappointed, but it was probably for the best. If a single level-up had healed every wound on my body, avoiding suspicion would have been difficult.

hunks.baseline: Even now, the physician kept stealing glances at me like I was a monster.
hunks.sol: Even now, the physician kept stealing glances at me as though I were a monster.

hunks.baseline: “Heavens. How bizarre. It’s far too much to pin on the effects of hundred-year snow ginseng…”
hunks.sol: “Heavens. How bizarre. This is far too much to attribute to the effects of hundred-year snow ginseng…”

hunks.baseline: Seeing how lost I looked, the physician explained. He was one of the few NPCs who knew I had lost my memory.
hunks.sol: Seeing my confusion, the physician explained. He was one of the few NPCs who knew I had lost my memory.

hunks.baseline: “It isn’t something you can get just because you have money, after all. You stole an elixir that can grant twenty years of internal energy in a single dose and consumed it.”
hunks.sol: “It isn’t something you can obtain simply by having enough money, after all. You stole and consumed an elixir capable of granting twenty years of internal energy in a single dose.”

hunks.baseline: At the same time, I felt a pang of regret. At the last moment, when I used the Skill, most of the twenty years of internal energy from the hundred-year snow ginseng had vanished.
hunks.sol: At the same time, a pang of regret washed over me. At the last moment, when I used the Skill, most of the twenty years of internal energy from the hundred-year snow ginseng had vanished.

hunks.baseline: It had been a complete disaster, because the energy had run wild instead of following my control.
hunks.sol: The whole disaster had happened because it ran wild instead of obeying my control.

hunks.baseline: *I used it as a one-time item.*
hunks.sol: *I blew it all on one use.*

hunks.baseline: The physician misread the look on my face and hurriedly added,
“Of course, Young Master, you must have made that decision for some grand purpose.”
hunks.sol: The physician misread the look on my face and hurriedly added, “Of course, Young Master, you must have made that decision for some grand purpose.”

hunks.baseline: The snow ginseng’s internal energy had kept me alive, but it was still a waste.
hunks.sol: The snow ginseng’s internal energy had kept me alive, but it was still such a waste.

hunks.baseline: A waste so bad it was killing me.
hunks.sol: Damn, what a waste.

hunks.baseline: The moment I saw it, pride welled up.
hunks.sol: The moment I saw it, pride welled up inside me.

hunks.baseline: It felt like only yesterday I’d been shaking in front of some two-bit bandits. Now I was a master in my own right. My Level had jumped after I took down Jopil, and I’d gained a massive amount of Fame.
hunks.sol: It felt like only yesterday I’d been trembling in front of a few two-bit bandits. Now I was something of a master in my own right. My Level had shot up after I took down Jopil, and I’d gained a massive amount of Fame.

hunks.baseline: That wasn’t all. I’d absorbed some of the hundred-year snow ginseng’s leftover energy and gained another four years of internal energy. On top of that…
hunks.sol: That wasn’t all. I’d absorbed some of the hundred-year snow ginseng’s remaining energy and gained another four years of internal energy. On top of that…

hunks.baseline: *I can adjust how much it consumes, and how much power it puts out.*
hunks.sol: *I can adjust how much it consumes and how much power it puts out.*

hunks.baseline: Thrust with All My Might. This Skill, now named One Flash, couldn’t be spammed. It could put out destructive power several stages above my usual level for an instant, but that single blow burned through all my strength.
hunks.sol: Thrust with All My Might. This Skill, now named One Flash, couldn’t be used recklessly. It could unleash destructive power several stages above my usual level for an instant, but that single blow would exhaust all my strength.

hunks.baseline: *No. Maybe it was always a Skill you could adjust.*
hunks.sol: *No. Maybe it was always a Skill I could adjust.*

hunks.baseline: In the real world, I was an F-rank Hunter. My physical abilities and the mana in my body were pathetic. But this game—Murim—was different.
hunks.sol: In the real world, I was an F-rank Hunter. My physical abilities and the mana in my body were pathetic. But in this game—in Murim—I was different.

hunks.baseline: Here I was a martial artist with fifteen years of internal energy and a body better than NPCs with a twenty- or thirty-Level gap. Change the vessel that holds the power, and the Skill’s original range of use comes out.
hunks.sol: Here, I was a martial artist with fifteen years of internal energy and physical abilities superior to NPCs twenty or thirty Levels above me. Changing the vessel that held the power had revealed how versatile the Skill had always been.

hunks.baseline: It felt like only yesterday Hyuk Mujin had been wiping the floor with me while I learned martial arts. Now I’d taken down a Peak master.
hunks.sol: It felt like only yesterday Hyuk Mujin had been wiping the floor with me while I struggled to learn martial arts. Now I’d taken down a Peak master.

hunks.baseline: Outside the window, they chanted my name several times a day.
hunks.sol: Outside the window, people chanted my name several times a day.

hunks.baseline: Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, hero of the family, that sort of thing.
hunks.sol: Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. Hero of the family. That sort of thing.

hunks.baseline: I never thought I’d hear a word like that in my life. For a two-bit F-rank Hunter whose motto was safety first, it was a word that had never had anything to do with me.
hunks.sol: I never thought I’d hear a word like that in my life. For a lowly F-rank Hunter whose motto was safety first, it was a word that had never had anything to do with me.

hunks.baseline: I lay still and fidgeted with my hands. Palms that had once been a young master’s—white and soft—were now packed tight with calluses.
hunks.sol: I lay still and wiggled my fingers. The palms that had once belonged to a pampered young master—white and soft—were now covered in calluses.

hunks.baseline: All told, the people I’d taken down numbered more than a few dozen. Bandits, wandering martial artists, even people rated as First Rate—and I had survived. I’d even taken down a Peak master I thought I could never beat: Jopil, One Question, One Kill.
hunks.sol: All told, the people I’d defeated numbered more than a few dozen. Bandits, wandering martial artists, even people rated as First Rate—and I had survived. I’d even taken down a Peak master I thought I could never beat: Jopil, One Question, One Kill.

hunks.baseline: If he was right, I was definitely strong. I’d survived every enemy I’d faced so far, and they were calling me a hero.
hunks.sol: If he was right, I was definitely strong. I’d survived every enemy I’d faced so far, and people were calling me a hero.

hunks.baseline: Yes. If I’m being honest…
hunks.sol: Yeah. If I was being honest…

hunks.baseline: *It doesn’t feel bad.*
hunks.sol: *It didn’t feel half bad.*

hunks.baseline: I ate and slept in a one-room goshiwon barely ten square meters across,[^1] the breadwinner who had to support my family. I couldn’t become a hero, and I didn’t want to.
hunks.sol: I ate and slept in a one-room goshiwon barely ten square meters in size,[^1] a breadwinner responsible for supporting my family. I couldn’t become a hero, and I didn’t want to.

hunks.baseline: I was just Jin Taekyung, a bottom-rung Hunter who fought every day praying he’d survive.
hunks.sol: I was just Jin Taekyung, a bottom-rung Hunter who fought every day while praying he would survive.

hunks.baseline: I’d done a lot of things F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung could never do. At the very least… I could protect the people who trusted and followed me from the enemy. People acknowledged me. They called me a hero.
hunks.sol: I’d done many things that F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung could never have done. At the very least… I could protect the people who trusted and followed me from their enemies. People acknowledged me. They called me a hero.

hunks.baseline: Even if everything here was nothing but virtual, even if the people in front of me were NPCs, that fact didn’t change.
hunks.sol: Even if everything here was nothing but virtual, even if the people before me were NPCs, that fact didn’t change.

hunks.baseline: Thinking that, I suddenly laughed.
hunks.sol: The thought made me laugh.

hunks.baseline: Without realizing it, I’d found that I was enjoying living as Jin Taekyung, a martial artist of Murim. Because this was a game. Because it could turn every impossibility into a possibility.
hunks.sol: Before I knew it, I’d started enjoying life as Jin Taekyung, a martial artist of Murim. Because this was a game. Because it could turn every impossibility into a possibility.

hunks.baseline: Only two conditions left before I could log out. Time could take care of Fame. The more rumors about me spread, the more it would keep climbing.
hunks.sol: Only two conditions remained before I could log out. Time would take care of Fame. The farther the rumors about me spread, the higher it would climb.

hunks.baseline: The problem was something else.
hunks.sol: The real problem lay elsewhere.
